title: P-256 negation-class rho v9c: disjoint DP/routing fields, fixed-cap refusal and bounded-memory detection

claims.statement: For the unrestricted-production P-256 challenge Q=[x]P, including the identity Q, the fully specified negation-class distinguished-point rho of argument.md recovers the canonical scalar with success at least 0.39, using total classical work at most 2^(12939/100) = 2^129.39 target-group-operation equivalents at the protected C=1000 scalar AArch64 instruction normalization, with peak memory below 2^73 bytes. Architecture: negation classes {P,-P}, class key x, canonical member (x,|y|), doubling escape from the minimum-fingerprint class of the detected cycle, N'=N*R/(R-1), a global work meter that halts at W_max, 64-bit distinguished points, and 2^16 storage nodes under a 16-bit routing field with a fixed per-node cap, charged set-up and routing inside H1. Disjoint-field routing spec: the key is the full 256-bit class key K=x; the DP predicate at width b tests mix64((K mod 2^64) XOR DPSALT) mod 2^b == 0 and therefore reads only key bits 0..63, while the router computes mix64(((K >> 128) mod 2^64) XOR RSALT) >> 48 and therefore reads only key bits 128..191, giving 16 bits and 2^16 nodes; the two fields are disjoint and independently mixed, mix64 is a bijection on 64-bit words, so at width 64 the predicate pins exactly one value of bits 0..63 and leaves the routing field free, and the routing collapse of the earlier same-field construction cannot occur. A 150000-key census at the production DP and route widths through this exact code reaches 58884 of 65536 nodes with max load 11 against an expected 2.2888 and a 2^-30.74 union bound at tolerance 24, 1.5 million keys attain all 65536 route values, and the same-field control collapses to 1 node with load 150000. Fixed-cap refusal: each node cap is fixed before the run from the declared expected report count, cap = max(1, ceil(5.087772 * declared_reports / nodes)); a report finding its node full is refused, counted, flags the trial cap-loss and is neither stored, matched nor overwritten, and every pipeline cell runs that path with zero cap violations. Bounded detector: a 2-slot fingerprint ring compares fp(K) with fp(K-2) and one checkpoint register carries the running minimum fingerprint of the previous 64-step block, so detector state is O(1) per trail - 2^16 trails x 4 entries x 136 bytes = 2^25.09 bytes - with no visited set, no history scan and no minimum-select over history. Complete step price: the transition canon(2X+T_j) is priced as the two batched affine additions X+(X+T_j) it actually is - core 4M+2S+12A = 1484, batch-inversion products 2 slots x 3M = 1320, batched Fermat inversion share 2, coefficient update 63, canonicalisation of y 14, degeneracy tests 12, bounded cycle detection 16, conditional negation of both coefficients after canonicalisation 2 x 24 = 48, itemised control 128, total 3087 instructions = 3.087 units, with M=220, S=176, A=21 itemised and no margin layered on the rows. Ledger: phase 1 = 3.087*(S_ops+2^60) = 2^129.279171 for S_ops = ceil(1.10*sqrt(2N'ln(1/0.60))) = 2^127.652966, reports 2^63.652966 x 128 instructions = 2^60.687, setup 2^25.045, total 2^129.279171; every row repriced by 6/5 gives 2^129.542206; the claim 129.39 leaves total <= claim - 0.10 and stays below the 129.46 live frontier at dispatch. Escapes are arrivals: a doubling of at most 1620 instructions consumes one step slot priced at 3087, so every escape is charged in full inside S_ops and no escape rate is assumed. Reports: the 64-bit DP condition gives expected 2^63.652966 reports <= 2^64 = a quarter of the 2^66-record, 2^72-byte capacity; Chernoff puts cap loss below 2^-8.8e19 and per node below 2^-100 after a 16-bit union bound, which is also the refusal debit. Success: modelled success at S_ops is 1-0.60^1.21 = 0.4610; the bounded toy runs the production protocol end to end (bounded detector, disjoint-field router, fixed-cap refusal, DP endpoint matching, exponent reconstruction, exact [x]P=Q verification) and measures 0.4275 on q26 at dp=6 with 144 of 8209 reports refused in 84 of 400 trials (0.4350 with refusal disabled), 0.4750 at dp=4, 0.4150 on the wide R=1024 table, 0.8900 at twice the budget, 0.4275 on q22, and 0.4153 at 8x volume where refusals fall to 0.29% with recovery identical to the no-refusal replay; walk efficiency is 0.864-0.919, so the claim is 0.39. Zero verification mismatches in every cell. ord_r(2)=N is even, so the shortest sign-ambiguous doubling gap is N/2 = 2^126.414*S_ops. The toy's out-of-regime dp=9 cell (0.0000 with the fixed cap, 0.2325 without) and the declared cap-stress cells are reported as adverse, not filtered. This is a supported exploratory analytic heuristic claim, not a theorem, a production run, a measured P-256 kernel price, an official score, novelty or a practical attack.
